why_this_matters: Day 124 sits in Phase 7 (Statistics), whose goal is: Describe data, quantify uncertainty and test hypotheses correctly. Today's core material - Statement and conditions, CLT for means, proportions and sums, Simulation experiments with skew and small n - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: 1. ONe-way ANOVA
code.code:
import scipy.stats as stats

# Sample data

a = [2.3, 3.4, 4.5, 2.3, 3.4]
b = [11.2, 12.2, 13.2, 12.2, 12.3]
c = [22.3, 23.4, 24.5, 22.3, 23.4]

# perform one-way ANOVA
f_stat, p_val = stats.f_oneway(a, b, c)

# print the results base on if else conditions
if p_val > 0.05:
    print(f'p-value: {p_val}, Means are equal (fail to reject H0)')
else:
    print(f'p-value: {p_val}, Means are not equal (reject H0)')

code.heading: 3. Paired Sample t-test
code.code:
import scipy.stats as stats

# sample data
before = [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
after = [3, 4, 5, 6, 7]

# perform paired sample t-test
t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_rel(before, after)

print("t-statistic:", t_stat)
print("p-value:", p_val)

# print the results using if else conditions
if p_val > 0.05:
    print(f'p-value: {p_val}, before mean is equal to after mean (fail to reject H0)')
else:
    print(f'p-value: {p_val}, before mean is not equal to after mean (reject H0)')

code.heading: 1.  Levene's Test
code.code:
import scipy.stats as stats

# Sample data
group1 = [2.3, 3.4, 4.5, 2.3, 3.4]
group2 = [1.2, 2.2, 3.2, 2.2, 2.3]

# Perform Levene's Test
w_stat, p_val = stats.levene(group1, group2)

print("w-statistic:", w_stat)
print("p-value:", p_val)

# print the results based on if else conditions
if p_val > 0.05:
    print(f'p-value: {p_val}, Variances are equal (fail to reject H0)')
else:
    print(f'p-value: {p_val}, Variances are not equal (reject H0)')

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Statement and conditions on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
